entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares it and no release this port builds exports it, but the route that would answer it does not work, MEASURED on the 6.1.3 release itself through xmake emulate: a decompression session created with kVTVideoDecoderSpecification_RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoDecoder is not the release's answer to whether a codec can be hardware-decoded. Per codec, with and without the key: H264 -12906/-12906, MPEG4 -12906/-12906, JPEG 0/-12906, HEVC -12906/-12906, ProRes422 -12906/-12906, where -12906 is kVTVideoDecoderMalfunctionErr and the only codec that got as far as the question is the one that SUCCEEDS without the key and FAILS with it. This release offers no query for the question at all: _VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported arrived with iOS 11 and _VTDecompressionSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionaryForDecoder does not exist at any band the port builds (4.3, 6.0, 6.1.3, 7.0.1, 10.3.4, 12.0, 16.0, 18.0)
entries.effect: owed: the row moves when a release this port builds can be asked. Everything measured so far says it cannot, and the host answers 1 for H264, HEVC, JPEG, ProRes422 and AV1 and 0 for MPEG2, VP9 and Animation on this Mac, with VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(VP9) moving 0 -> 1 after VTRegisterSupplementalVideoDecoderIfAvailable
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:321-331 for the declaration; the per-band ladder from tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua over ~/.charon/dyld/4.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 and the 6.1.3 dump, and coordination/corpus/caches/*.tsv; this host's own answers (H264 1, HEVC 1, MPEG2 0, JPEG 1, ProRes422 1, AV1 1, VP9 0) in the facts page

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares it at VTVideoEncoderList.h:60 and the release has no such symbol (zero hits for _VTCopySupportedPropertyDictionaryForEncoder in the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. Everything it returns is the RELEASE's own and is asked for rather than assembled: the encoder ID is the compression session's kVTCompressionPropertyKey_EncoderID read back through the release's VTSessionCopyProperty, and the property dictionary is the release's VTSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary for that session. The ENCODER ID half is narrower than it looked: kVTCompressionPropertyKey_EncoderID is a NULL POINTER at both bands this port builds - dump-cache.lua finds no _kVTCompressionPropertyKey_EncoderID in the 4.3 or the 6.1.3 armv7 cache, and the port's own build gate says the same ('weakly imports 1 symbol the armv7 release it is checked against does not export, each of which is NULL there and must be called only behind a check for it'). An encoder ID is an iOS 11 idea, so at 4.3 and at 6.1.3 the release has no such property and there is nothing to read
entries.effect: the release's key set with the release's per-key attribute dictionaries - measured on this host, 2026-10-03: H264 gives 140 keys with 0 NULL values, each value an attribute dictionary such as { PropertyType = Number; ReadWriteStatus = ReadWrite; } of which 45 are the EMPTY dictionary; HEVC 169 with 43 empty; ProRes422 59 with all 59 empty; JPEG 54 with 52 empty. A codec with NO encoder answers kVTCouldNotFindVideoEncoderErr (-12908) with no encoder ID and no dictionary, measured for MPEG2 and AV1, and NOT an empty dictionary; kVTParameterErr for a width or height of zero or less; at 4.3 and at 6.1.3 *encoderIDOut is left NULL with the status still noErr, because that band has no encoder ID to give - the release's answer rather than an accident of a missing key. A NULL encoderSpecification is turned into an EMPTY dictionary before VTCompressionSessionCreate, because the 6.1.3 release answers a NULL one with kVTParameterErr (-12902), measured for H264 and MPEG4 through xmake emulate, while this host's VTCompressionSessionCreate accepts both a NULL and an empty specification for H264 with noErr and a session either way
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTVideoEncoderList.h:55-64 for the declaration and VTErrors.h:37 for -12908; the release's own VTSessionCopyProperty (VTSession.h:112) and VTSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary, both present in the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 caches
